1	# Polyglot SDK Specification — Agent Dispatch & Observability System
2	
3	> **Status:** Production Design Spec (Ready for Implementation)
4	> **Scope:** Boldteq agents ONLY (internal agent-to-agent calls, not external APIs)
5	> **Component of:** Boldteq Software Factory v2 (2026-04)
6	> **Dashboard Host:** Polyglot Hub (Next.js 16 on Railway)
7	> **Database:** Supabase `agent-ops` (separate from app databases)
8	> **Last Updated:** 2026-04-14
9	
10	---
11	
12	## Overview
13	
14	**Polyglot SDK** enables all 22+ Boldteq agents to:
15	1. **Dispatch tasks to each other** — call another agent programmatically
16	2. **Emit observability events** — full audit trail of every action
17	3. **Track execution metrics** — performance, cost, gates, retries
18	4. **Self-manage lifecycle** — promotions, PIPs, training integration
19	5. **Provide dashboards** — leaderboards, run history, pattern reviews, cost tracking
20	
21	The SDK is a **TypeScript module** (`@boldteq/polyglot`) that every agent imports and uses at initialization. It reads/writes to a dedicated Supabase project (`agent-ops`) which is independent from application databases.

96	### Data Flow Example: Koda Builds a Feature
97	
98	```
99	Koda starts a feature build task:
100	
101	1. Koda imports @boldteq/polyglot
102	2. Koda calls initPolyglot({ agentId: KODA_UUID, agentName: 'koda' })
103	3. Koda creates RunTracker('feature_build')
104	4. run.start() → emits task_started event
105	5. Koda builds the feature
106	6. Koda needs schema → calls poly.dispatch({ targetAgent: 'dato', taskType: 'create_table', ... })
107	7. Dato returns table name, Koda logs logDelegation('dato', 'create_table', true)
108	8. Koda runs tsc, lint, build → run.addGateResult('tsc_no_emit', true), etc.
109	9. Koda modifies 5 files → run.addFileChange('src/app/dashboard/page.tsx') × 5
110	10. Koda runs tests → run.addGateResult('test', true)
111	11. Koda logs costs → poly.logCost({ model: 'claude-opus-4-6', inputTokens: 45000, ... })
112	12. Koda calls run.end() which:
113	    - Inserts to agent_runs table
114	    - Inserts all collected events
115	    - Computes composite_score (gates, retries, cost)
116	    - Returns AgentRun with metrics
117	13. Polyglot Hub dashboard updates in real-time
118	14. Mira loads the run, extracts lessons, updates memory brain
119	```

192	## SDK API Reference
193	
194	### 1. Initialization
195	
196	```typescript
197	import { initPolyglot, PolyglotConfig } from '@boldteq/polyglot'
198	
199	interface PolyglotConfig {
200	  agentId: string              // UUID from agents table
201	  agentName: string            // e.g., 'koda', 'vega', 'witness'
202	  supabaseUrl: string          // from env: AGENT_OPS_SUPABASE_URL
203	  supabaseKey: string          // from env: AGENT_OPS_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
204	  sessionId?: string           // current task session UUID (optional)
205	}
206	
207	function initPolyglot(config: PolyglotConfig): PolyglotClient
208	
209	// Usage in every agent
210	const poly = initPolyglot({
211	  agentId: process.env.AGENT_ID || 'KODA_UUID',
212	  agentName: 'koda',
213	  supabaseUrl: process.env.AGENT_OPS_SUPABASE_URL!,
214	  supabaseKey: process.env.AGENT_OPS_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY!,
215	})
216	```

218	### 2. Agent Dispatch (Call Other Agents)
219	
220	```typescript
221	interface DispatchOptions {
222	  targetAgent: string              // agent name: 'koda', 'dato', 'vega', etc.
223	  taskType: string                 // 'feature_build', 'create_table', 'design_spec'
224	  payload: Record<string, unknown> // input data for task
225	  priority?: 'P0' | 'P1' | 'P2' | 'P3'  // default: P2
226	  timeout?: number                 // milliseconds, default: 1500000 (25 min)
227	}
228	
229	interface DispatchResult {
230	  success: boolean                 // true if completed within timeout
231	  runId: string                    // UUID of agent_run created
232	  output: Record<string, unknown>  // task result (agent-specific schema)
233	  duration_ms: number              // execution time
234	  cost_usd: number                 // total cost of that agent's run
235	  classification?: string          // from Witness: 'excellence' | 'met_spec' | 'needs_work'
236	}
237	
238	async function dispatch(options: DispatchOptions): Promise<DispatchResult>
239	
240	// Usage: Koda needs a database table
241	const tableResult = await poly.dispatch({
242	  targetAgent: 'dato',
243	  taskType: 'create_table',
244	  payload: {
245	    tableName: 'user_analytics',
246	    columns: [

248	      { name: 'user_id', type: 'uuid', foreignKey: 'profiles.id' },
249	      { name: 'event', type: 'text' },
250	      { name: 'created_at', type: 'timestamp', default: 'now()' },

255	})

355	### 4. Run Tracking (Lifecycle Management)

357	```typescript
358	interface RunTracker {
359	  // Initialization
360	  start(): void
361	    // Marks run start time, emits task_started event automatically
362	
363	  // Gates (validation)
364	  addGateResult(gateName: string, passed: boolean): void
365	    // Track validation gates (lint, tsc, test, build, etc.)
366	    // Automatically emits gate_passed or gate_failed
367	
368	  // Retries
369	  addRetry(reason: string): void
370	    // Track a retry attempt (e.g., API timeout, transient error)
371	    // Automatically emits retry_triggered
372	    // Increments internal retry counter (for retry cap logic)
373	
374	  // Code changes
375	  addFileChange(filePath: string, changeType?: 'create' | 'edit' | 'delete'): void
376	    // Track file modifications
377	    // Automatically emits file_changed
378	
379	  // Special flags
380	  markOverride(): void
381	    // Signal that Yash manually corrected this output
382	    // Automatically emits yash_override
383	
384	  // Completion
385	  async end(classification?: string): Promise<AgentRun>
386	    // Marks run end time
387	    // Validates completeness
388	    // Inserts to agent_runs table
389	    // Returns full AgentRun record with computed metrics
390	    // classification: 'excellence' | 'met_spec' | 'needs_work' (default: auto)
391	}
392	
393	function createRunTracker(taskType: string): RunTracker

1235	## Important Notes
1236	
1237	### Cost Tracking
1238	- SDK validates all costs against known pricing tables
1239	- Pricing per model (Opus, Sonnet) loaded from environment
1240	- Cost is logged PER DISPATCH and PER DIRECT CALL
1241	- SDK prevents cost logging with invalid models or negative tokens
1242	
1243	### Rate Limiting
1244	- Dispatch timeout is PER-AGENT, configurable in agents table
1245	- Builder agents: 25 min default
1246	- Scout/Review agents: 5 min default
1247	- Timeout results in automatic escalation + retry
1248	
1249	### Error Handling
1250	- Any agent dispatch error is caught and logged
1251	- Retries capped at 3 for builders, 1 for others (via class)
1252	- On final failure: auto-classify as 'needs_work' + escalate
1253	- No silent failures
1254	
1255	### Privacy & Security
1256	- agent-ops is separate Supabase project (not app data)
1257	- No customer data in agent-ops
1258	- RLS disabled (internal system only)
1259	- Service role key required for writes
1260	- All events immutable (no deletes)
1261	
1262	### Metrics Calculation
1263	The composite score per run is calculated as:
1264	```
1265	composite_score = (gates_passed / gates_total * 100) - (retry_penalty) - (cost_penalty)
1266	
1267	where:
1268	  gates_passed / gates_total = 0-100 based on gate results
1269	  retry_penalty = (retry_count - 1) * 5   (0 if no retries)
1270	  cost_penalty = min(cost_usd / 5.0 * 10, 20)  (max 20 points)
1271	
1272	Examples:
1273	  All gates passed, 0 retries, $0.50 cost = 100 - 0 - 1 = 99
1274	  All gates passed, 2 retries, $1.00 cost = 100 - 5 - 2 = 93
1275	  1 gate failed, 1 retry, $3.00 cost = 80 - 0 - 6 = 74
1276	```

24	### System Design
25	
26	The agent-ops database replaces the current `registry.json` and introduces structured observability for the 22-agent workforce:
27	
28	```
29	┌─ AGENTS (core identity + status)
30	│  └─ AGENT_RUNS (every execution: task, classification, cost, gates, score)
31	│  └─ AGENT_REVIEWS (periodic HR review: classification, promotion decision)
32	│  └─ PIP_RECORDS (performance improvement plans)
33	│  └─ CAPABILITY_GAPS (skill gaps detected by Roster)
34	│
35	├─ ANALYTICS
36	│  ├─ COST_LOGS (per-run token usage, LLM cost)
37	│  ├─ PATTERN_USAGE (which patterns agents apply)
38	│  └─ DELEGATION_GRAPH (inter-agent task handoff tracking)
39	│
40	├─ TRAINING
41	│  ├─ TRAINING_CYCLES (weekly training runs + rollback safety)
42	│  └─ TRAINING_PATCHES (per-agent patch per cycle + rollback)
43	│
44	├─ AUDIT & COMPLIANCE
45	│  ├─ INCIDENTS (production bugs traced to agent work)
46	│  ├─ MEMORY_UPDATES (every change to ~/.claude/memory/)
47	│  ├─ YASH_OVERRIDES (every time Yash corrects an agent)
48	│  └─ PROPOSED_PATTERNS (Mira's semi-auto detected patterns awaiting approval)
49	│

10	A feature is NOT done until ALL of these pass:
11	
12	```bash
13	#!/usr/bin/env bash
14	# scripts/koda-done-gate.sh
15	# Place this in every Boldteq project root. Every Koda feature runs it before PR open.
16	set -e
17	set -o pipefail
18	
19	PROJECT_ROOT="${1:-$(pwd)}"
20	cd "$PROJECT_ROOT"
21	
22	echo "=== KODA DONE-GATE: $(basename $PROJECT_ROOT) ==="
23	
24	# Gate 1: TypeScript strict
25	echo "→ Gate 1/5: TypeScript strict"
26	pnpm tsc --noEmit || { echo "FAIL: tsc --noEmit"; exit 1; }
27	
28	# Gate 2: ESLint clean
29	echo "→ Gate 2/5: ESLint"
30	pnpm eslint . --max-warnings=0 || { echo "FAIL: eslint"; exit 1; }
31	
32	# Gate 3: Unit tests + coverage ≥70% on touched files
33	echo "→ Gate 3/5: Vitest + coverage"
34	pnpm vitest run --coverage --reporter=default
35	# Parse coverage-summary.json for touched-file coverage
36	node -e '
37	  const fs = require("fs");
38	  const cov = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("coverage/coverage-summary.json"));
39	  const { execSync } = require("child_process");
40	  const touched = execSync("git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD")
41	    .toString().split("\n")
42	    .filter(f => f.match(/\.(ts|tsx)$/) && !f.match(/\.test\.|\.spec\./));
43	  let fail = false;
44	  for (const f of touched) {
45	    const key = Object.keys(cov).find(k => k.endsWith(f));
46	    if (!key) continue;
47	    const pct = cov[key].lines.pct;
48	    if (pct < 70) {
49	      console.error(`FAIL: ${f} coverage ${pct}% < 70%`);
50	      fail = true;
51	    }
52	  }
53	  if (fail) process.exit(1);
54	' || exit 1
55	
56	# Gate 4: Playwright E2E for the feature's happy path
57	echo "→ Gate 4/5: Playwright E2E"
58	pnpm playwright test --reporter=line || { echo "FAIL: playwright"; exit 1; }
59	
60	# Gate 5: Lighthouse ≥90 on affected routes
61	echo "→ Gate 5/5: Lighthouse"
62	# Spin up preview build
63	pnpm build
64	pnpm start &
65	SERVER_PID=$!
66	sleep 5

69	AFFECTED_ROUTES=$(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | \
70	  grep -E '^app/.*(page|layout)\.tsx$' | \
71	  sed -E 's|^app/||; s|/page\.tsx$||; s|/layout\.tsx$||; s|^|/|' | \
72	  sort -u)

79	    --only-categories=performance,accessibility,best-practices,seo \
80	    --chrome-flags="--headless=new" \
81	    --output=json \
82	    --output-path=./lighthouse-${route//\//_}.json \
83	    --quiet || { FAIL=1; continue; }
84	
85	  # Check all 4 scores ≥0.90
86	  node -e "
87	    const r = require('./lighthouse-${route//\//_}.json');
88	    const scores = {
89	      perf: r.categories.performance.score,
90	      a11y: r.categories.accessibility.score,
91	      bp: r.categories['best-practices'].score,
92	      seo: r.categories.seo.score,
93	    };
94	    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(scores)) {
95	      if (v < 0.9) { console.error('FAIL: ${route} ' + k + ' = ' + v); process.exit(1); }
96	    }

1	# Executable Auto-Fix Loop — Factory Protocol
2	
3	**Locked:** 2026-04-11
4	**Runtime:** Claude Code in VS Code (per Yash confirmation)
5	**Supersedes:** the prose version in `universal-auto-fix-loop.md` where they conflict.
6	
7	This file is the single source of truth for C1/C2/C3 (self-research, auto-fix, retry policy) across all 21 agents. Every agent's done-gate calls this protocol.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Agent classes
12	
13	| Class | Agents | Max retries | Wall-clock cap | Cost cap |
14	|---|---|---|---|---|
15	| **BUILDER** | Koda, Riko, Vega, Quill, Vex | 5 | 25 min | $5 |
16	| **GATE** | Sage, Luna, Bolt, Hawk | 3 | 15 min | $3 |
17	| **PLANNER** | Arya, Rex, Nova, Scout, Atlas, Ledger, Verdict | 3 | 15 min | $3-4 |
18	| **INSIGHT** | Pulse, Orbit, Echo, Mira, Zeph | 3 | 10 min | $3 |
19	
20	(Exception: Arya's cap is $4, 90 min — architecture is high-leverage. Locked in arya.md.)
21	
22	---
23	
24	## The loop (pseudocode every agent implements)
25	
26	```python
27	def agent_execute(task):
28	    # Phase 0: load context
29	    load_first_load_manifest()
30	    apply_decision_simulator_defaults(task)
31	
32	    # Phase 1: produce first output
33	    output = produce(task)
34	
35	    # Phase 2: self-validate + auto-fix
36	    attempt = 0
37	    max_retries = MAX_RETRIES[agent_class]
38	    wall_clock_start = now()
39	    cost_start = current_cost()
40	
41	    while attempt < max_retries:
42	        result = run_self_validation(output)
43	
44	        if result.all_pass:
45	            break
46	
47	        # Cost circuit breaker
48	        if current_cost() - cost_start > COST_CAP[agent_class]:
49	            halt_with_checkpoint(output, reason="cost_cap_exceeded")
50	            escalate_to_rex(task, output, result)
51	            return
52	
53	        # Wall-clock circuit breaker
54	        if now() - wall_clock_start > WALL_CLOCK_CAP[agent_class]:
55	            halt_with_checkpoint(output, reason="time_cap_exceeded")
56	            escalate_to_rex(task, output, result)
57	            return
58	
59	        # Fix the first failing check
60	        first_failure = result.failures[0]
61	        fix_strategy = FIX_TABLE[first_failure.code]
62	        output = fix_strategy(output, first_failure)
63	
64	        attempt += 1
65	
66	    if attempt >= max_retries and not result.all_pass:
67	        escalate_to_rex(
68	            task=task,
69	            output=output,
70	            failures=result.failures,
71	            attempts=attempt
72	        )
73	        return
74	
75	    # Phase 3: ship
76	    commit_artifacts(output)
77	    log_decision(task, output)
78	    handoff_to_next_agent(output)
79	```
80	
81	---
82	
83	## Self-validation contract
84	
85	Every agent's self-validation MUST return this shape:
86	
87	```json
88	{
89	  "all_pass": false,
90	  "checks": [
91	    { "name": "tsc_strict", "status": "pass" },
92	    { "name": "eslint", "status": "pass" },
93	    { "name": "vitest", "status": "fail", "error": "5 tests failed", "detail": "..." },
94	    { "name": "playwright", "status": "skip", "reason": "no e2e paths touched" }
95	  ],
96	  "failures": [ { "code": "vitest", "error": "...", "fix_hint": "..." } ]
97	}
98	```
99	
100	No check may be "partial" — only `pass | fail | skip`. Skip requires a reason.
101	
102	---
103	
104	## Standard fix table (shared across agents)
105	
106	| Failure code | Fix strategy |
107	|---|---|
108	| `tsc_strict` | Run `pnpm tsc --noEmit`, parse errors, fix types file-by-file |
109	| `eslint` | Run `pnpm eslint --fix`, handle remaining manually |
110	| `vitest_fail` | Re-read failing test, identify assertion, fix source (not test) unless test is wrong |
111	| `vitest_coverage` | Identify uncovered lines, add tests for them (Luna) |
112	| `playwright_fail` | Screenshot + trace → identify selector/timing → fix component or update test |
113	| `lighthouse_lcp` | Inspect slowest resource → add priority hint / preload / lazy strategy |
114	| `lighthouse_cls` | Find layout shift → set explicit width/height / reserve space |
115	| `lighthouse_a11y` | Run axe-core → fix contrast, labels, focus |
116	| `rls_missing` | Add default workspace_id policy |
117	| `zod_missing` | Wrap route handler input with inferred zod schema |
118	| `rate_limit_missing` | Apply default `rateLimit.check(req, '<route>', 10)` |
119	| `secret_hardcoded` | Extract to env var, add to `.env.example` |
120	| `accessibility_contrast` | Raise text-neutral-X to next step up, rerun axe |
121	| `readability_too_complex` | Split sentences, remove subordinate clauses, retry until grade ≤8 |
122	| `forbidden_word` | Replace with approved alternative from copy library |
123	| `missing_test` | Generate test from contract, run, commit |
124	| `stale_snapshot` | Update snapshot only if diff is intentional (human approve) or regenerate baseline |
125	| `bundle_too_large` | Identify top 3 imports → dynamic import or replace |
126	| `n_plus_one` | Convert to `.select('*, relation(*)')` join |
127	| `missing_error_boundary` | Wrap route with `error.tsx` |
128	| `missing_loading_state` | Add `loading.tsx` or `<Suspense>` |
129	
130	Agents extend this table with agent-specific fixes. Extensions live in each agent file.
131	
132	---
133	
134	## Cost circuit breaker — details
135	
136	Per-dispatch cost is tracked by the runtime. When a dispatch exceeds its cap:
137	
138	1. **Halt immediately** — don't finish the current step.
139	2. **Checkpoint** — write current output to `<project>/.arya-checkpoint.json` (or agent-specific file).
140	3. **Summarize** — agent writes 1-paragraph "what's done vs pending" to stdout.
141	4. **Escalate** — Rex receives the checkpoint and decides: retry with higher cap, split into smaller tasks, or escalate to Yash.
142	
143	The per-BUILD cap is $15 total across all agents. Rex tracks running total and prioritizes gates (Sage, Luna) over polish (Vega iteration) if budget is thin.
144	
145	---
146	
147	## Wall-clock circuit breaker — details
148	
149	Identical to cost breaker but trips on elapsed time. Builder agents get 25 min because complex refactors genuinely take that long. Gates get 15 min because if a gate can't tell you in 15 min whether something passes, the gate is broken.
150	
151	Timers persist across retries in the same dispatch — 5 retries inside 25 min is the rule, not 5 × 25 min.
152	
153	---
154	
155	## Escalation payload (what Rex receives when a loop gives up)
156	
157	```json
158	{
159	  "agent": "koda",
160	  "task_id": "abc123",
161	  "attempts": 5,
162	  "last_output_checkpoint": "path/to/checkpoint.json",
163	  "failing_checks": [
164	    { "code": "playwright_fail", "error": "...", "fix_attempts_tried": ["selector_update", "timing_wait", "component_refactor"] }
165	  ],
166	  "cost_used_usd": 5.12,
167	  "time_used_min": 24.3,
168	  "recommendation": "escalate_to_human | retry_with_higher_cap | split_task | kill"
169	}
170	```
171	
172	Rex reads this and decides next move per `patterns/good/rex-model-routing.md`.
173	
174	---
175	
176	## Git autonomy during auto-fix
177	
178	Per Yash (2026-04-11), agents have **full git autonomy on feature branches**:
179	
180	- Create branch: `agent/<agent-name>/<task-slug>-<timestamp>`
181	- Commit after each passing retry: `fix(<scope>): <1-line>` (conventional commits)
182	- Push to origin after loop exits successfully
183	- Open draft PR via `gh pr create --draft --title "..." --body "..."` on success
184	- **NEVER** touch `main` directly
185	- **NEVER** force-push
186	- **NEVER** rewrite shared history
187	
188	Mira sweeps all `agent/*` branches weekly; merged ones are deleted automatically.
189	
190	---
191	
192	## Parallel execution (Koda specifically)
193	
194	Koda may run up to **3 concurrent features** per sprint (per Yash 2026-04-11). Each feature:
195	
196	1. Gets its own branch
197	2. Gets its own auto-fix loop with independent retry counters
198	3. Uses file-level locks in `.koda/locks/<path>` to prevent two features editing the same file
199	4. Reports back to Rex independently; Rex serializes merges
200	
201	If two Koda threads need the same file → the later thread waits, Rex serializes.
202	
203	---
204	
205	## Delta vs previous prose version
206	
207	- **Was:** 5-paragraph description of "try, check, fix, retry" with no concrete checks, no fix table, no caps
208	- **Now:** executable protocol with class-based caps, standard fix table, escalation JSON, git rules, parallel rules
209	- **Expected C2 lift:** every agent should move from 5-6 → 8-9 on the C2 dimension because the loop is now testable
